value.rationale: The allocation of a fixed number of random-walk observations across two convex hulls is a canonical optimization of an exact stochastic-geometric observable. The result shows a provably unbounded O(sqrt N) deviation from proportional sampling for all unequal fixed multiplicities, with a strict universal sign and near-uniqueness of the optimal integer allocation. This is a structural finite-discretization effect absent from the continuous-time Brownian formula; no unrelated downstream applications are asserted.
